chunks: God abrogates or confirms whatsoever He will, for He has with Him the Book of Books.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book (divine source/record)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Umm al-Kitab and how does God abrogate or confirm?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is central to the doctrine of *al-Naskh* (abrogation), distinguishing between the eternal, unchanging record in *Umm al-Kitab* and its temporal manifestation in the created world. It underscores that divine decrees are not arbitrary but follow a precise, pre-ordained wisdom, where what is 'wiped out' or 'established' reflects the unfolding of God's will in time. This concept reinforces the belief in divine omniscience and the ultimate justice of Allah, as all changes are recorded and known to Him.
